questions.question: What is a summary?
options: A short retelling of a text's main points in your own words
A copy of the most important sentences from the text
Your personal opinion about a text
A list of difficult words in the text
questions.explanation: A summary gives only the main points, in your own words, and is much shorter than the original - usually one third or less.

questions.question: Should you include your own opinions in a summary?
options: No - a summary should be objective
Yes - opinions make it more interesting
Only if you disagree with the author
Yes, but only in the first sentence
questions.explanation: A summary is objective: it reports what the text says without adding your own views.

questions.question: What should you leave OUT of a summary?
options: Small details and examples
The main points
The text's main message
The most important ideas
questions.explanation: A summary includes only the main points. Details, examples and minor information are left out.

questions.question: Why must a summary be written in your own words?
options: Copying sentences is plagiarism and does not show that you understood the text
The original words are always wrong
Your own words are always shorter
It is faster to write
questions.explanation: Using your own words shows understanding and avoids plagiarism. Copying sentences from the original is not summarising.

questions.question: Which is a good way to start a summary?
options: "The text is about..." or "The author describes..."
"I think this text is boring because..."
"Once upon a time..."
"Dear reader,"
questions.explanation: Useful starting phrases include "The text is about...", "The author describes..." or "The main point of the article is...".
